_doc: Run-wide survivor tuning (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md sections 5, 6; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4.4). Everything here is tier C (ours / emulator-like) unless a note says otherwise; canonical WZ numbers are never copied here except where noted as a survivor choice of equipment.

exp_curve._formula: Tier C #293 first-pass training: round(4 + 8*L^2), minimum 1; L1 12, L7 396, L49 19212. Faster opening and steeper late costs; canonical EXP unchanged.

mob_skills._doc: Tier C: enabled boss kits; slow x retains x percent of upgraded speed; defense x adds flat defense; heal restores the canonical x (y unused, no roll); 140 is timed self weapon immunity; attack_up_mult is the timed weapon-attack multiplier of Attack Up 100 (self) / 110 (area) on touch and physical attackN damage, after Threaten and before boss dmg_mult (the v83 x115 is not read).

mob_projectiles._tier: tier C: swept body contact radius when the canonical ball has no lt/rb; 320 px/s fallback only when bulletSpeed is absent/nonpositive (Jr. Balrog). Authored positive bulletSpeed keeps its existing conversion.

mob_attacks._doc: Tier C (#76): ordinary (non-boss) mobs use their canonical Mob.wz attackN (damage, range, attackAfter unchanged). interval = seconds of on-screen, fully visible time between one mob's attack starts (WZ has no attack interval; the first wait is 50-100% of it by spawn identity); dmg_mult scales the canonical MADamage/PADamage (default 1.0, unscaled like contact damage; elites also take stages elites.damage_mult). First-pass values chosen before measurement, not tuned (#77).

combat._doc: Tier C (#166/#200): linear projectile pierce decay keeps at least this fraction of its damage; the shipped default is 10%. Tier C (#364): negative fractions rise up to pierce_ceiling (200%).

player._start: Tier C: survivor starter stats, the v83 Beginner 50 HP. There is no MP (ADR 0006). The skills a round starts with are per job (survivor/jobs.json start_skills, #284).
player._fortune: Tier C: card-tier odds only; equipment/NX sources are deferred. This is separate from canonical LUK.
player._ap: Tier C: 5 automatic AP per level (AutoAp). ap: one row per job, {primary, secondary, keyframes} (#284, ADR 0006: no weapon paths, no redistribution on advancement); a job without its own row uses its nearest ancestor's, no row at all puts every AP into STR. Earned AP first fills the secondary stat up to its base-value target at the character's level (keyframes [{level, target}], linear, floored, held outside their range), the rest goes to the primary. 212 (owner, spec #282): INT primary, LUK secondary at about level + 2 (the v83 Magician equipment pattern: reqLUK 15 at Lv13, 30 at Lv28, 40 at Lv38, 70 at Lv68). The other rows keep the unported lines' skill tests meaningful until each line is ported: 200 the Magician lines; 100 the Warrior (all STR, #163); 300 the Bowman (DEX, STR level+5 through Lv30, STR35 through Lv34, STR40 at Lv35, level+5 through Lv70, #199/#202/#203); 400 the Thief (LUK, DEX max(25, level), #207); 510 / 520 the Brawler (STR, DEX = level) and Gunslinger (DEX, STR = level, #186/#189).
player._equipment: Worn equipment comes from the character (creation outfit, later drops); stats are canonical asset-cache info. No job grants a weapon (#284). inventory_slots, tier A: a new v83 character Equip tab.
player._body: Touch hitbox relative to the feet (x, y, w, h), roughly the v83 character's body + head.
player._cast: Targeting measures from cast_height px above the feet; shots start cast_forward px further toward their target (the throwing hand, in front of the body).

growth._100: Tier B: Warrior HP 24-28 per level (Cosmic levelUp, v83-facts 4), fixed midpoint 26; Improved MaxHP Increase adds its own HP per level-up on top.
growth._300: Tier B (#199): Bowman HP20-24 per level, fixed midpoint 22 (v83-facts4).
growth._400: Tier B (#207): Thief per-level HP 20-24, fixed midpoint 22 (v83-facts 4); existing accumulated-total rounding.
growth._500: Tier B (#186): Pirate per-level HP 22-28, fixed midpoint 25 (v83-facts 4). Accumulate fractional growth and round the total as for other jobs.

_level_up_refill: Fraction of the new maximum HP restored on each level-up, after that level's growth. HP 0.0: tier C, owner choice for difficulty.
_hit_window: Spec #88, tier C (ours): the grace after a landed hit. lengths: the window after the 1st, 2nd, 3rd... chained landed hit, the last held (lengths[0] is the full window, which a boss skill attack always starts). chain_gap: a landed hit this soon (s) after the previous landed hit steps to the next shorter length; after reset_after (s) without a landed hit the chain restarts at lengths[0]; between the two the step holds. Boss skill attacks ignore the window (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md Constants and provenance).
_portals: Same-map portals only: activation box relative to the portal point, lift above arrival before falling, global cooldown in seconds. Tier C: owner choice; source and destination points stay canonical.
_mesos: Meso drops (#107). Per-mob ranges are survivor data in mobs.json ("mesos": [min, max), tier B: v83 server drop data). chance: tier B reference (v83 servers drop a meso entry 40% of the time at rate 1); mult scales every amount, tier C (set once from an estimate: the only Henesys clear in the smoke (random policy, seed 1, 3259 kills, all three bosses) earned 22.9k mesos at mult 1, so 14 gives about 320k, the owner's 300-350k target for a clear (the sensible bot dies at 13-15 min with about 15k at mult 1; see docs/GAME_DESIGN.md 4.2 #107; NX upgrades, #34, may raise it later; it is not tuned further here). boss_drops: tier C, bundles a scheduled boss's death drops, each rolled from its range (bosses always drop, there is no chance roll). fallback: tier C, mobs without a v83 range roll around base + per_level x mob level, low/high x that centre (fitted to the v83 early-roster ranges: level 1 = 4-6, level 22 = 28-42, level 50 = 60-90).
_mob_speed_factor: mob move speed px/s = (speed stat + 100) x this x stage speed (MobKind.SPEED_SCALE is the same 0.625; a different value here rescales every mob)
_mob_motion: tier C: flyer vertical bob amplitude in pixels and period in seconds; pursuit still uses canonical flySpeed through mob_speed_factor
_regen: Tier B: recovery comes in 10-second pulses (the v83 cadence). Tier C: always recover 10 HP per pulse; hp_regen modifiers and every owned skill's `regen` field (skills.json, Loadout.regen_bonus) add to each pulse.
_crit: Tier C: every job and damage type, including Beginner, fixed skills and basic attacks, can crit. per_acc is a small untuned placeholder: +0.05 percentage points per ACC. Passive crit damage adds skill-percentage points instead of multiplying (tier B: SouthPerry Critical Shot/Throw).
_pickup: EXP drops: pop speed and sideways spread (px/s), magnet start speed (px/s) and acceleration (px/s^2), live drop cap (the farthest from the player is absorbed into a fresh drop at each new kill), lifetime (s an uncollected drop lies before it expires, its EXP lost; 0 = never) and fade (its last seconds, fading out). They fall with Physics.img gravity/fallSpeed.

bot._engage: Tier C (#162): melee-aware movement. A build whose longest attack (active job-line skills via SkillRunner.reach_of, or the held weapon swing via BasicAttack.reach; Beginner skills only when it has none of its own) reaches less than kite_reach px walks up to the nearest on-level mob within chase_range px and stops at reach_fraction of its longest ready attack, facing it; below retreat_hp of max HP, or while a boss attack winds up, it kites like every other build. Longer-reach builds (every Magician attack reaches 260+) keep the kiting bot unchanged.
bot._doc: Tier C #293: card_scores are base overrides (no job bonus). New actives 100, active ranks 74; passive bases retain #289 ordering. After three held actives BotInput adds 20 to common passives so useful global boosts beat ordinary ranks. Mastery scores its actual diminished bonus at 100 points per unit; ordinary rarity bonuses and extra magnitude use gain_step_score 6. Random policy stays uniform. Tier C (spec #296, H9 #305): the seven Hero pool skills (power_strike, slash_blast, brandish, shout, monster_magnet, panic, coma) score like every other pool skill, new 100 and rank 74, whatever their cast rule, so the meter-gated finishers (Panic, Coma) and the pull (Monster Magnet), which the default scorer would not take for attacks, are taken.
bot._equipment_weights: Tier C (spec #33, #112): how much a bot values each inc* stat of an equipment instance (an item scores the sum of weight x value; stats not listed are worth 0). Keyed by job id ("0" Beginner, "200" Magician; a job uses its own entry, else its nearest ancestor's through the job lineage, so second jobs inherit their first job's); a job line without an entry falls back to the Beginner's. A Magician wants M.ATT, then INT (LUK a little), then defences (M.DEF over W.DEF), then pools and movement. The bot wears the best wearable item per slot at each equipment pickup and level-up (BotInput.auto_equip); BotShop also reads the weights to pick scrolls and to keep or sell spare equipment.
bot._equipment_bowman: Tier C (#199): PAD first, DEX primary and STR secondary; defence/pool/movement weights follow the existing physical baseline, untuned.

_potions: Tier C (spec #237): unlimited potions, separate shared cooldowns, level-driven items and bot drink thresholds. No stock or drops. Restore amounts come from each current item's canonical spec.

potions._cooldown: Tier C (spec #237): unlimited potions; an HP cooldown in sim seconds, shared by player and pet.
potions._bot: Tier C: drink only when the missing HP is at least min_restore_fraction of one current potion's canonical restore, with the restore capped at the max HP pool but counted as at least pool_floor of the potion (owner: waste guard for small pools; the cap keeps the 1000-2000 point steps of #229 drinkable, tier C).
potions._schedule: Tier C (ours): automatic potion upgrades by character level (spec #225, replacing the potion-tier cards). Each step {level, kind hp, item} makes the kind's current potion that item once the character reaches the level (sim, at level-up with a notice, and silently on snapshot load); the cooldown is kept, a step never downgrades, and an item without a canonical restore spec is skipped. Sorted by level. The first two are the old card gates (Orange @10, White @25; the MP steps went with MP, ADR 0006). The next two are researched steps, each tier C (docs/research/v83-potion-progression.md section 6, ticket #229): Unagi 2022003 (1000 HP) @40, Ice Cream Pop 2001001 (2000 HP) @60. The levels are our own reading of thin sources (no source names when players moved to the Lv 60 foods), and the step is job-agnostic, so a small pool wastes the overheal. Restore amounts are never typed here: they come from each item's canonical spec in Item.wz (Consume/0200.img, 0202.img); an old asset cache without these items simply stops at the last tier it holds.
potions._plural_names: Tier C (ours, spec #225 review): optional plural display names for the level-up notice, keyed by item id. A scheduled item without an entry reads String.wz name + 's' ('Your Red Potions are now Orange Potions.'); this name is its own plural.

_spawn: SpawnDirector (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md 4): margin outside the view, band of the first spawn ring and band_y, how far it reaches above and below the view (the floors beside the view; -1 = band), min distance to the player, samples per ring, recycle distance (px) and time (s) of the far/unreachable relocation rule, prefer_route (a ring first looks for a point whose NavGraph travel cost to the player is at most half the view width + margin + this many px; -1 = any reachable point), stall_time (s an off-screen mob may go without coming stall_progress px closer by moving itself before it is relocated ahead of the player; 0 = never), trail_margin (px the margin grows on the side the player moves away from: the camera lags about 29 px behind a running player).
_bosses: Tier C: warning/placement/pressure, stalled-pursuit fade relocation, canonical EXP reward multiplier and shower geometry, bonus choice count; stage entries may override rewards. arrival_fallback (#260): seconds an arrival (or a stalled-pursuit relocation) may keep failing for want of a point on the player's platform before it uses the platform of the floor nearest the player instead.
_run_time_cap: Tier C: balance/full-run harness timeout, allowing the finale to continue beyond 15:00.
_nx_award: Tier C #293 first pass: per_level 2 to offset more levels per round, clear/boss amounts unchanged; the frozen balance pass revisits these. NX paid at the end of every round. A clear pays clear_bonus[tier] + per_level x levels gained in the round + per_boss x scheduled bosses killed in the round; a death pays the same without the clear bonus. clear_bonus is indexed by the stage's 0-based tier (later tiers reuse the last entry). Deletion, Quit round and tool rounds are never credited.
